currentContext.expansion: The headline expansion event of FY 2025-26 was the commercial commissioning of the Company's plastic pipes and fittings facility at Roorkee, Uttarakhand in January 2026. The plant was commissioned and capitalised with an initial capacity of 12,500 tonnes per annum, taking total installed plastic pipes and fittings capacity to 78,500 tonnes per annum across Sangareddy (Telangana) and Roorkee, and establishing a manufacturing presence in North India that improves regional market access and logistics reach. Alongside the physical capacity addition, the pipes business broadened its addressable market by introducing advanced foam core and double-wall corrugated piping solutions (for below-ground sewerage applications) and by adding in-house PTMT bath fittings manufacturing — a backward-integration step launched commercially during the year to secure greater quality and supply-chain control and to strengthen the rural-market presence. In Bathware, installed manufacturing capacity comprises sanitaryware of up to 1.75 million pieces per annum at Bahadurgarh, Haryana and up to 2.1 million pieces per annum at Bibinagar, Telangana, and faucets of up to 3.7 million pieces per annum at Kaharani, Rajasthan; no new bathware capex project is announced. Management states that the major expansion-phase capital expenditure is now fully complete, so the forward priority shifts from building capacity to optimising invested capital — driving higher capacity utilisation across the manufacturing network and scaling core and value-added product lines to support margin expansion. In parallel, the Company restructured its manufacturing footprint to release capital: in December 2025 it divested the joint venture's (Hintastica Private Limited) manufacturing facility in Telangana and used the proceeds to fully repay outstanding debt, deleveraging the joint venture and accelerating the transition towards a flexible, asset-light framework. Corporate-structure-wise, the Board-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement will demerge the Consumer Products Business into wholly-owned subsidiary HHIL Limited and amalgamate the remaining Company into Hindware Limited, with both entities to be listed on BSE and NSE; the appointed date is 1 April 2025 and the Scheme awaits NCLT sanction.

risks.note: Exposure to macroeconomic slowdowns, global market disturbances, war-related disruptions, geopolitical tensions, inflation spikes and interest-rate hikes, all of which can dampen consumer demand for what is largely a discretionary, housing-linked product basket. Mitigated by diversifying across business segments, optimising cost structures, broadening the customer base and monitoring global developments.

risks.risk: Competition risk, including from unbranded and online-first players
risks.note: Intensifying competition, particularly from unbranded players, can erode pricing power and compress margins; in kitchen appliances the entry of online-first brands and value-led imports has intensified channel fragmentation and pricing pressure. Mitigated through R&D and product innovation and an omnichannel distribution network.

Rapid shifts in consumer preferences may lead to lower adoption of products if the Company fails to adapt, and shorter product lifecycles in appliances demand continuous design innovation. Mitigated by a structured consumer-feedback mechanism that tailors product offerings.

Shifts in buying habits may undermine traditional distribution channels, impacting revenue and profitability — material for a business whose moat is a general-trade dealer and retailer network. Mitigated by an omnichannel strategy combining a strengthened e-commerce presence with continued investment in traditional channels.

risks.risk: Operating efficiency and supply chain risk
risks.note: Under-utilisation of logistics, retail and support assets, plus unexpected supply chain disruptions, can inflate costs, delay product availability and reduce margins — a live issue given newly commissioned capacity that must be filled. Mitigated by optimising logistics and store operations, automation and a franchise model to improve coverage and resource utilisation.

risks.risk: Product quality and brand legacy risk
risks.note: Poor quality can damage sales and brand reputation, and misleading or negative perceptions across media channels can detract from brand equity — a heightened exposure for a six-decade household brand. Mitigated by rigorous quality-control standards with continuous audits and supplier oversight, and integrated communication strategies.

risks.risk: Credit profile and credit rating risk
risks.note: Difficulty securing short- and long-term funds at favourable rates can strain liquidity and hamper operations, while fluctuations in the credit profile can raise the cost of capital or restrict financing access. Mitigated by optimising working-capital cycles, maintaining well-staggered debt maturities and transparent lender/rating-agency relationships.

Volatility in foreign exchange rates can erode profitability on imports and exports; the Company imports raw materials, spare parts and components. Mitigated by hedging strategies including forward and option contracts.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence and cyber security risk
risks.note: Reliance on outdated technology may erode competitiveness, while cyber-attacks could disrupt operations and compromise data integrity. Mitigated by investing in state-of-the-art equipment, partnering with global technology leaders, technology scouting, resilient IT infrastructure, penetration testing and staff training.

one-line thesis: Hindware executed a strategic pivot by exiting loss-making consumer categories (coolers, fans) to focus on high-margin bathware and pipes, driving consolidated EBITDA up 27% YoY despite flat revenue. Guidance for FY27 targets 15-20% growth in bathware and volume recovery in pipes, underpinned by new capacity commissioning and premium product mix shifts.
financial scorecard: Revenue: ₹2,510cr (FY26) vs ₹2,523cr (FY25), flat YoY; EBITDA: ₹233cr (+27% YoY), Margin 9% (vs 7%); PAT: Pre-tax profit ₹45cr vs loss ₹28cr (FY25), impacted by ₹52.6cr exceptional item (JV goodwill impairment & shutdown costs); Order Book: Pipes had strong orders but executed only ~50% in March due to inventory constraints; Net Debt: ₹708cr (consolidated), reduced in Bathware to ₹234cr but increased in Pipes to ₹429cr due to capex.
guidance: Bathware Revenue Growth: 15-20% (FY27); Pipes Volume Growth: 14-15% (FY27); Margins: Systematic expansion of 150-200 bps annually for next 2 years; Consumer Appliances: Targeting ₹100cr/quarter run-rate by Q1/Q2 FY27; Capex: Roorkee plant ramping, utilization to scale in H2 FY27.
order book & pipeline: Pipes business reported strong order inflows but faced execution bottlenecks in March (only 50% fulfillment) due to raw material scarcity; April saw 50% YoY growth indicating pent-up demand release.
segment / subsidiary detail: Bathware: Rev ₹1,520cr (+10%), EBITDA margin 10.3% (+160bps); Pipes: Rev ₹673cr, EBITDA ₹41cr, PBT loss ₹29cr due to RM volatility and lean inventory strategy; Consumer Appliances: Rev ₹317cr, Negative EBITDA ₹12cr (strategic exit from coolers/fans ongoing).
growth verticals / optionality: Tier 2/3 distribution expansion; Premium brand 'Queo' and 'Italian Collection' mix shift; AI-enabled chimneys launch; Roorkee pipe plant full utilization in H2 FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Input cost inflation (Brass +33%, Gas, PVC resin spike to ₹114/kg) offset by price hikes (Faucets +15% in Jan, +3% in May; Sanitaryware +6% in Feb, +7% in April); Margin expansion driven by premiumization and operating leverage.
capex / expansion: Roorkee pipe plant operational Jan 2026; Focus shifting from expansion to debottlenecking and efficiency; Future capex limited to maintenance and efficiency upgrades.
capital allocation: Debt reduction priority: Targeting 30-40% net debt reduction over next 2 years (₹145-150cr repayment planned immediately); Working capital days improved to 89 (Bathware) from 103.
risks & watch-items: Raw material volatility (PVC, Brass, Gas); Real estate slowdown in affordable housing segment; Execution risk in Roorkee plant ramp-up; Competitive intensity in top 5-6 organized players.
management quality / tone: Confident on strategic pivot; Disciplined on cost/pass-through; Optimistic on FY27 volume recovery; Transparent about one-off impairments.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite revenue stagnation, the quality of earnings improved drastically via portfolio pruning; The 'loss' in Pipes PBT is largely timing-driven due to voluntary lean inventory during price spikes, not structural demand failure; JV impairment (Hintastica) is a one-off cleanup to enable future profitability.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Building Products business comprises bathware, faucets, premium tiles and plastic pipes and fittings, run on an optimum mix of in-house manufacturing and strategic outsourcing and sold through a deeply entrenched retail and dealer network across residential, institutional and e-commerce channels nationwide. The Consumer Products vertical extends the Hindware brand into the modern home with a focused kitchen range of chimneys, cooktops, hobs, sinks and water heaters, distributed through dedicated trade, modern retail and digital channels. The two businesses operate as independent verticals, each positioned to accelerate growth and optimise its own specialised supply chain, and the Board has approved a Composite Scheme of Arrangement to separate them into two listed entities.

products.body:

- **Tiles:** GVT tiles (Glossy Sinker, Velvet Sinker, Honed Travertine, Anti-Skid R10, Paper Matt), Platform tiles, RX-600 Extro tile adhesive, RX-700 Extro Flex tile adhesive, Tile cutting tools
- **Plastic Pipes and Fittings:** CPVC and PVC pipes and fittings, Foam core pipes, Double-wall corrugated pipes, PTMT bath fittings
- **Consumer Products:** Chimneys (BLDC and AI-enabled), Cooktops, Hobs, Sinks, Water heaters

- Consumer preferences are shifting towards premium, aesthetically designed and technology-enabled solutions — the core driver of the premiumisation mix lever
- Institutional and project sales contributed approximately 25% of Bathware segment turnover, giving a well-diversified channel profile alongside general trade and e-commerce
- Government programmes — Swachh Bharat Mission, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, PMAY and Smart Cities Mission — sustain capital deployment into sanitation, housing and municipal water networks
- In pipes, declining PVC resin prices weighed on realisations and margins and caused inventory losses and cautious channel behaviour, before demand improved in H2 as prices stabilised and dealer restocking resumed
- Structural pipes demand comes from high-rise residential proliferation, more water outlets per housing unit, stringent BIS compliance norms and the shift away from conventional metal pipes towards CPVC
- Consumer Products demand was dented by inflationary pressure and cautious discretionary spending, while long-term support comes from urbanisation, rising disposable incomes and evolving lifestyles
- Kitchen appliances competition intensified from online-first brands and value-led imports, fragmenting channels and pressuring pricing and product lifecycles
- Management expects the streamlined Consumer Products portfolio, optimised cost structure and smart-appliance launches to unlock operating leverage and a stronger profitability trajectory in the periods ahead
- India's growth is expected to moderate to around 6.6% in FY 2026-27, with RBI forecasting inflation around 4.6%, supporting resilient domestic demand
- Currency fluctuations and inflation raise the landed cost of imported raw materials and components, while higher household living costs pressure discretionary spending
- Bathware entered FY 2026-27 with operational momentum from sustained brand investment, an expanded active dealer network and broad-based growth across general trade, institutional and e-commerce channels
- The Roorkee commissioning added regional reach in North India and, together with high-margin product introductions, broadened the addressable market

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Input cost inflation (Brass +33%, Gas, PVC resin spike to ₹114/kg) offset by price hikes (Faucets +15% in Jan, +3% in May; Sanitaryware +6% in Feb, +7% in April); Margin expansion driven by premiumization and operating leverage.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction priority: Targeting 30-40% net debt reduction over next 2 years (₹145-150cr repayment planned immediately); Working capital days improved to 89 (Bathware) from 103.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The headline expansion event of FY 2025-26 was the commercial commissioning of the Company's plastic pipes and fittings facility at Roorkee, Uttarakhand in January 2026. The plant was commissioned and capitalised with an initial capacity of 12,500 tonnes per annum, taking total installed plastic pipes and fittings capacity to 78,500 tonnes per annum across Sangareddy (Telangana) and Roorkee, and establishing a manufacturing presence in North India that improves regional market access and logistics reach. Alongside the physical capacity addition, the pipes business broadened its addressable market by introducing advanced foam core and double-wall corrugated piping solutions (for below-ground sewerage applications) and by adding in-house PTMT bath fittings manufacturing — a backward-integration step launched commercially during the year to secure greater quality and supply-chain control and to strengthen the rural-market presence. In Bathware, installed manufacturing capacity comprises sanitaryware of up to 1.75 million pieces per annum at Bahadurgarh, Haryana and up to 2.1 million pieces per annum at Bibinagar, Telangana, and faucets of up to 3.7 million pieces per annum at Kaharani, Rajasthan; no new bathware capex project is announced. Management states that the major expansion-phase capital expenditure is now fully complete, so the forward priority shifts from building capacity to optimising invested capital — driving higher capacity utilisation across the manufacturing network and scaling core and value-added product lines to support margin expansion. In parallel, the Company restructured its manufacturing footprint to release capital: in December 2025 it divested the joint venture's (Hintastica Private Limited) manufacturing facility in Telangana and used the proceeds to fully repay outstanding debt, deleveraging the joint venture and accelerating the transition towards a flexible, asset-light framework. Corporate-structure-wise, the Board-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement will demerge the Consumer Products Business into wholly-owned subsidiary HHIL Limited and amalgamate the remaining Company into Hindware Limited, with both entities to be listed on BSE and NSE; the appointed date is 1 April 2025 and the Scheme awaits NCLT sanction.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on strategic pivot; Disciplined on cost/pass-through; Optimistic on FY27 volume recovery; Transparent about one-off impairments.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "As per information provided by the Company to its Secretarial Auditors, there are no pending cases filed by or against the Company which will have a major impact on the Company.", "as_of": "2026-07-25"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Six-decade brand legacy — established in 1960 and the first to introduce vitreous china sanitaryware in India, making Hindware an iconic household name
- Deeply entrenched, multi-channel distribution spanning general trade, institutional, modern retail and e-commerce nationwide
- In-house manufacturing across four locations combined with strategic outsourcing, giving capacity plus flexibility
- Trade and influencer ecosystems that are hard to replicate — over 1,00,000 plumbers enrolled under the Plumber No. 1 programme and the Club Maestro architect loyalty platform
- Position among the top five brands in key categories, supported by rigorous quality-control standards, continuous audits and supplier oversight
- Brand architecture spanning premium to entry price points (Hindware, Queo), enabling targeted premiumisation
- Backward integration into in-house PTMT bath fittings manufacturing for greater quality and supply-chain control
- In-house facilities to develop all its technology

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material volatility (PVC, Brass, Gas); Real estate slowdown in affordable housing segment; Execution risk in Roorkee plant ramp-up; Competitive intensity in top 5-6 organized players.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite revenue stagnation, the quality of earnings improved drastically via portfolio pruning; The 'loss' in Pipes PBT is largely timing-driven due to voluntary lean inventory during price spikes, not structural demand failure; JV impairment (Hintastica) is a one-off cleanup to enable future profitability.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Drive premiumisation across the product portfolio at key price points, in Bathware, Tiles and Consumer Products alike
- Optimise internal cost structures and pursue rigorous cost management to protect margins
- Execute the Composite Scheme of Arrangement to create two independently focused pure-play entities — Hindware Limited (Bathware plus Plastic Pipes and Fittings) and HHIL Limited (Consumer Products) — and list them separately
- Shift towards a flexible, asset-light framework: restructure manufacturing footprints to release capital, as done with the December 2025 divestment of the joint …

challenges.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] Board-approved Composite Scheme of Arrangement: "demerger of the Consumer Products Business into wholly-owned subsidiary HHIL Limited and amalgamation of the remaining Company into Hindware Limited". Post-implementation both HHIL Limited and Hindware Limited will be listed on BSE & NSE and "Hindware Home Innovation Limited will cease to exist".
- [Demerger - entitlement] "Shareholders holding 1 share in Hindware Home Innovation Limited will receive 1 share in HHIL Limited and 1 share in Hindware Limited." Appointed date is 01st April 2025.
- [Demerger - status] Approvals received from BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange; "The Scheme received requisite approval from the unsecured creditors, equity shareholders of the Company and unsecured creditors of the Transferee Company during their respective NCLT convened meetings held on 7 March 2026"; it remains "subject to such other necessary approvals... and sanction thereof by the NCLT".
- [Structure] Current group: listed Hindware Home Innovation Limited holds the Consumer Products Business directly, the Building Products Business "via 98.6% subsidiary Hindware Limited" (unlisted), plus 100%-held Hintastica Pvt. Ltd. (Water Heater), HHIL Limited and EHPL - the last marked "*Discontinued Business".
- [Channel mix] Bathware revenue is described as balanced: "Retail remained the primary contributor; institutional & project sales contributed ~25%, with both channels growing and supporting a diversified demand profile." Separately, two distinct boards are presented - Sandip Somany is Chairman & Managing Director of Hindware Limited but Chairman & Non-Executive Director of Hindware Home Innovation Limited - consistent with the pending two-entity split.
